steps.text: Make the cake: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray a 9-inch springform pan with floured cooking spray.
Beat 3/4 cup sugar and egg yolks in a mixing bowl with an electric mixer until light in color and doubled in volume. Stir in flour, milk, baking powder, and vanilla.

Beat egg whites in a glass or metal bowl until soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining 1/4 cup sugar, continuing to beat until medium peaks form. Fold 1/3 of the egg white mixture into the egg yolk mixture to lighten it. Fold in remaining egg whites, then pour batter into the prepared pan.

Bake in the preheated oven until a cake tester inserted into the middle comes out clean, 45 to 50 minutes. Cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes. Loosen the edges with a knife, then remove the sides. Let cake cool completely on the wire rack, about 20 more minutes.
Invert cake onto a deep serving plate and remove the pan bottom. Pierce the cake all over with a two-pronged meat fork or a cake tester.

Make the filling and topping: Mix condensed milk, evaporated milk, and 1/4 cup whipping cream together in a bowl. Measure 1 cup milk mixture and refrigerate for another use. Slowly pour remaining milk mixture over the cake until absorbed.

Pour remaining whipping cream into a chilled glass or metal bowl. Beat with an electric mixer until it thickens and reaches spreading consistency. Spread whipped cream over cake and garnish with cherries.
If not serving immediately, refrigerate until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Tres Leches Cake
raw_recipe.description: Try this tres leches cake recipe for a sweet and delicious dessert! A light sponge cake soaks up three types of milk and is frosted with whipped cream.
raw_recipe.name: Tres Leches Cake

review.reviewBody: This is a basic sponge cake recipe soaked in a milk mixture. A succesful sponge cake requires proper treatment of the egg, at every step. The egg whites form the body or lightness of the cake. It is extremely important to properly fold the whites into the batter. Too much folding and you have a flat cake. Too little folding and you will have "chewy" pieces from unincorporated egg white. The 1/4 c. granulated sugar should be added to the egg whites before whipping, as sugar helps build peaks, prevents overbeating, and dissolves in liquid egg. I don't know why some reviewers thought white sugar meant powdered sugar, but sponge cakes are made with granulated sugar. I substituted cake flour (1 c. + 2 T.), added a pinch of salt, and the cake was great.

Yum! Made this for my daughter's Spanish Fiesta at the end of the year. I read reviews, and poured milk mix on hot cake, worked beautifully. I have never made homemade whip cream before, but based on web search chilled beaters and bowl in freezer 20 min before whipping. Worked like a charm. Also used unflavored gelatin to stabilize the whip cream. Was good looking for next day, plus left overs on day 2. I made recipe as is, in 9 X 13 inch pan to send to school, my oven is fussy but I baked 20-25 minutes (seemed to be about right time for size of pan). It was just enough batter for cake to be good size at serving time. May have helped with soaking up milk too. I will verify this can all be made the night before, with excellent results. I have never had this but liked it, my daughter's friends liked it as well. Thanks!!

It is extremely important to properly fold the whites into the batter. Too much folding and you have a flat cake. Too little folding and you will have "chewy" pieces from unincorporated egg white. The 1/4 c. granulated sugar should be added to the egg whites before whipping, as sugar helps build peaks, prevents overbeating, and dissolves in liquid egg.

Pure Joy! My husband is Cuban and he was overjoyed to see this on his plate for dessert. This was my first attempt at Tres Leches and the recipe has suprisingly few ingredients. I was very exacting with the process of the recipe, especially how the eggs are handled. That resulted in a perfect "sponge" type cake that melts in the mouth. I will note that, being familiar with my husband's palette, I did double the amount of vanilla and I cannot imagine the recipe without that change. I used my "good vanilla" not the artificial and the cake did not taste "vanilla". I too added just a hint of sugar to the whipped cream because that is how I prefer my whipped cream. Those two changes did not overwhelm the recipe. This beautiful cake simply tasted rich and well balanced. Finally, for the baking, I used my springform pan and I think that worked out very well for handling the baked cake without damaging it and therefore the presentation of the finished cake.

I liked this cake a good amount but would change the following;
1. I used ALL of the milk mixture and added it while the cake was warm. Refrigerated afterwords till cold. Cake held together wonderfully
2. Would add a little cinnamon to the milk mixture for more flavor. It was a tad bland.
3. Find another way (besides adding cinnamon) to enhance flavor of milk mixture. The cake flavor was perfect.
Tip: tastes better after chilling overnight and adding sugar (2 TBSP) and vanilla (1tsp) to whipped cream topping.

This is a terrific recipe! Be sure to follow the instructions: mix egg yolk with sugar and dry ingredients before gently folding in beaten egg whites. I poured the milk over the cake a little at a time, allowing it to absorb evenly one spoonful at a time. The final cake could have absorbed additional milk mixture; next time I will try adding more and reserving less. It might be yummy with rum, amaretto, tuaca, or brandy added to the milk mixture. The recipe is correct with granulated sugar; I'm not sure why some reviewers say it should be powdered sugar.

I have searched for the perfect tres leches recipe, and I can now end my search! This recipe hit it right on. Some tips I would offer to 'first-timers' is:
When you fold in the egg whites, be very careful not to over-mix them in. If you must choose, under-mix them in, but overt mixing will result in flat-custard like cake-yuck! Secondly, This cake tastes better if you let it sit for a day or two in the fridge (the perfect make ahead dessert!) Only don't frost it until the day you serve it. The receipe said to trow out the remaining milk, but I like mine extra moist, so I saved it and added it on serving day, and the cake soaked it right up. Lastly, whip up the remaining cream with about 1/4 c sugar and 1 tsp vanilla for the frosting. Yum! Recipe says garnish with cherries, but I prefer lots and lots of fresh fruit and berries. Enjoy!

First time making tres leches and it was so good! Followed instructions and cake turned out perfect! What I did different:
- checked the cake after 30 mins and was done
- didn't wait for cake to cool down completely
- didn't poke any holes to the cake, milk mixture was absorbed evenly
- added a tsp of vanilla and almond extract to whipping cream before mixing
- added 1 cup of granulated sugar and 1/4 cup of conf sugar to whipping cream at the end. It has been almost a day and whipped cream still looks perfect.
- little cinnamon powder on top
Beautiful, easy, delicious!

I made a perfect mistake By adding 1.25 cups of sugar total to the recipe. 1 cup for the flour mixture and .25 cups of sugar for the heavy whipping cream mixture. I served this for Cinco and my whole office loved it. Some of them said it was the best cake they have ever had. I'm not a very good cook by any means but I have to give myself a pat on the back for this one. Enjoy!

This was an excellent recipe I made it for my daughter for her birthday today and for Thanksgiving. I did make a few changes to the milk adding 1 cup of whole milk in place 1/4 cup of heavy cream. I also added 1tbs of vanilla to the milk mixture. For the whip cream topping I added 1/3 cup of confectioners sugar and the entire pint (2 cups) of heavy whipping cream and whipped on medium/high speed until thick enough to spread on top. For a finishing touch I added some cinnamon on top just for a little color and added flavor. It came out perfect, my while family really enjoyed it!

I made this for my husband's birthday, and everyone loved it! The only thing I changed is I omitted the cherries. I added strawberries that I macerated for approximately 2 hours in 1/4 cup of sugar and 6 oz. pineapple juice. Absolutely delicious!

This recipe is simple and delicious. Very traditional, Mexican tres leches. It is always requested at family gatherings. Sometimes I’ll add almond or rum extract depending on what fruit or nut topping is used. Very versatile cake. Thanks for the wonderful recipe!

Made this for the first time ever using this recipe. I poured the leche over the hot cake very slowly, and refrigerated it after it cooled down a bit. Added cinnamon to the leche. Added the sugar and vanilla as suggested to the whipped cream. Took it to a party and it was a hit. So good!

Very easy to make. Delicious. Only thing i would change is adding a bit of sugar to the whipped cream to make it a bit sweeter, if it has no sugar its a little sour. I put dulce de leche on mine as a topping to make it a cuatro leches.
I divided the batter and made 2 nine inch round cakes, soaked them separately and put a layer of whipped cream in between.
Perfect recipe. I added strawberries on top instead of cherries.
Delicious. Making another one right away because the family begged.
